baseline.execution_environment: Separate GitHub-hosted Ubuntu VM and fresh Docker per suite; sequential backends within each suite

candidate.execution_environment: Separate GitHub-hosted Ubuntu VM and fresh Docker per suite; sequential backends within each suite

limitations: The official default PostHog warmup uses two API operations, while the earlier optimization goal used eight. Low backlog did not generalize; this run must not be described as confirmation of that goal.
The warmup difference is an observed experimental difference, not a proven explanation for the new PostHog backlog.

PostHog before/after reflects cumulative core and adapter changes: batched claim transactions, pending-record eligibility/index, direct completion update, separate worker scheduler, separate SMTP receiver for both backends, immediate claim checks after completion, and successful-completion backoff reset. The future-completion wakeup callback already existed in the baseline; these measurements do not isolate individual mechanisms.

PostHog historical warmup used one producer; the candidate uses the configured producer budget during its two warmup operations. Measured requests, native business APIs, task granularity and argument/output parity remain unchanged.
Different GitHub runs use different hosts. Celery also changes across runs; before/after percentages are not isolated causal measurements or statistical significance claims.
Saleor dbworker wall time regressed against the old main run and is slower than same-run Celery; this is retained without selective reruns.
Image scenarios have no comparable admitted task lifecycle metrics in this summary; unavailable metrics are omitted.
Execution concurrency measures overlapping task elapsed time, not CPU utilization. No cross-project overall throughput average is computed.
Complete native traces remain in the original CI artifacts and downloaded temporary directories; this compact file preserves identities, checksums and summary metrics only.
The local 32-worker capacity failures are separate experiments and are excluded from these official 8-worker scores.

metric_definitions.aggregation: Each displayed value is the median of three complete repetitions for that backend/scenario.
metric_definitions.mean_execution_span: Sum of handler execution durations divided by first-handler-start to last-handler-completion span.
metric_definitions.mean_measurement: Sum of handler execution durations divided by complete measured wall time.
metric_definitions.mean_published_outstanding_measurement: Sum of publication-to-completion durations divided by complete measured wall time.
metric_definitions.peak_published_outstanding: Peak already published unfinished tasks, including running tasks.
metric_definitions.peak_running: Instantaneous execution concurrency reconstructed from admitted native lifecycle timestamps.
metric_definitions.percent_change: 100 * (candidate / baseline - 1); descriptive across two different GitHub runs.
metric_definitions.queue_wait_p95_seconds: Publication to native handler start, including reservation and dispatch; nearest-rank P95 within each sample.
metric_definitions.wall_seconds: Total measured business window, including scheduled API submission and draining.

optimization_goal_generalization.reason: The separate warm8 PostHog goal result does not establish low backlog for the default warm2 official profile.

scope: One complete official six-suite full-profile run; no new runtime optimization
